The dots, while a very simple concept, gives kids a whole new reason to engage with books. It lets you make the reading experience more interactive and it the popping sound is quite satisfying.

Pros
- Well drawn
- High quality pages
- Bubbles seem like they'll stand up to abuse
- Largely good word choice

Cons
- They could have probably thought of some better words for some letters (e.g., Farmer Yumi for Y)

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Pass The Peas This game has a cute, creative format unlike anything I've seen for a word game. Everything about the game from the container, to the letter trays, and the letters themselves is related to peas. The cardboard trays are made to look like pea pods and the letters look like peas.

The container is a cylinder made of sturdy cardboard in which all the game pieces fit. The letters come in individual, green drawstring bag. If the game was played often, I'm not sure how long the letter trays would hold up, but other than that, everything does seem fairly durable.

Unfortunately, the game itself doesn't live up to the clever concept. Each player draws 10 letters from their bag of letters and has 30 seconds to make a word. Then all players "pass the peas" to the next player, who tries to use as many of their own letters to make a new word out of the original word passed to them. The only requirement is at least one of the original letters must be left remaining. For example, you can add an "S" to the beginning and an "S" to the end to make the word "TOP" into a new word "STOPS" or you can change "DUST" into "LINT" by replacing the "DUS" with "LIN".

The game sounds like it could be fun, but it is frustrating. I play online word games often, but still found it hard to think of a word using my letters and get them arranged on the tray within 30 seconds. It was also hard to make a new word when one of your opponent's trays was passed to you. I first played the game with just one other player and thought maybe adding another player would make the game more fun, but the main problem was the difficulty in making words and not the pace of the game, it wasn't any better with three players. After repeated games full of frustration, it became boring and nobody wanted to play any longer, which is a shame since the pea theme is so clever. An elementary school child might have fun ignoring the timer and the rules and just using the letters to make words since the game pieces are so cute.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Pass The Peas

Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+ I ADORE the idea of this kit! It is seriously awesome! There's no clean up whatsoever, so my little ones can "paint" and learn to their heart's content, and I don't have to worry about them staining clothes or painting the walls. If it was designed a bit sturdier, it would be an amazing "busy bag" item(without supervision).

When these cards first came in the mail, I saw that there was a white sticker(of sorts) over the card. Getting this sticker wet makes the picture show up. I knew without supervision, that sticker could be torn up quickly or logged with water. I sat with my boys as they took turns "painting" the cards. They were gentle! Still, as the sticker dried, I saw more and more scratches showing up, which means the picture underneath is no longer hidden(though you can still pretty much see what it's going to be anyway...the white sticker doesn't hide it 100% even with no scratches) I was disappointed that it ended up being so fragile.

I recommend letting your little one have a large space, so that he/she doesn't have to stack the cards together as they dry. We were on the porch the first time my boys used them, and I lay them individually on the porch rail. I stacked them when we came in the house, though. I'm sure that is part of the scratching problem. Unfortunately, that leaves out the places that this kit would come in most handy, like car rides, doctor waiting rooms, and church(for especially young ones). It also makes the key ring that is included pretty worthless.

The little brush is two pieces. You simply unscrew the top, fill it with water, and then put it back together. It worked well, and we didn't have issue with leaking.

Overall, once again, I absolutely adore the idea of this kit, but I wish the cards weren't so fragile.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White This is a four star product in many ways. But I'm giving it three due to the following factors...

Excellent build quality and hardware features. However, without some additional software and accessories this you won't see lasting use.

Hardware: you WILL need a phone or tablet to unlock the limited potential of this toy. The included gesture and sound functionality is too rudimentary (and yet also hard to acess consistently) for lasting interest. If you don't plan to provide access to a tablet or phone, get WowWee's robotic dog product instead. Although it is easy to set up an obstacle course or seesaw on your own, purpose-built accessories would go a long way towards providing a "fiction" for the toy to inhabit, as well as proven fun activities.

Software: the existing apps are very well made and provide a significant boost to the toys functionality. I'd say about 75%. However, most are of limited scope and soon become repetitive. The best feature is the ability to remotely drive the robot and also record its adventures. I'd like to see a feature that allows kids to rudimentarily program the robot (perhaps to interact with purpose built accessories) not just activate sounds and colored lights... I'd also like to see the toolset opened to adults (Lua scripting?) so that they can extend the functionality for Pre-K through K STEM learning.

I understand trying to hit price points is important. But this is either a $75 toy with a few $25 accessory kits, or a $125 toy all in. The existing package (while decent) is limiting the potential of the product.
text_fidelity_b: WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack OK...so here's the deal with these...
5 stars for how much my 17mo old son LOVES them.
3 stars for how the crayon is constantly coming out of the plastic holder.
Averages to...4 stars.
No one is really addressing a few things, so I will...
these are super bright, amazing, soft crayons that are each a very distinct & different color.
In our particular tub, they color perfectly...but we have a somewhat "satin" finish as opposed to the shiny white finish which is what I imagine is the problem for people who say they don't work. I notice they color fantastically on dry or "damp" tub surfaces...but not as well on truly wet, slick surfaces.
We have a clear silicone table mat with a scene silkscreened on that I sometimes wet the back of and slap on the tub wall so he can color away on it like a coloring book page. Again, the crayons work perfectly when the surface is dry or damp, but can't get grippy enough for the color to stick when it's slick wet.

These crayons do constantly come out of the holders but I just keep pushing them back in. They also push back into the holder because the button is where my son grips the crayons in his tiny hands but when that happens he just moves on to another one, since there are 5.

I put these in to a bag of goodies I gave him for Valentine's Day and ours are still going strong with daily...prolific...color & scribble use on the tub, his tub toys, his picture mat, himself, and Mommy....head to toe. He does lots of "body art" with these, and he enjoys using his scrubby sponge for clean up and erasing his handywork, as much as he does the coloring part!

To me...these babies are worth their weight in gold if you have a budding artist on your hands, the right kind of tub surface, and teach the little virtuoso how to scrub it all clean to start with a fresh canvas! We LOVE...and I mean...LOVE them, and I can't see us ever being without them as my son is pretty much obsessed with all things artistic, and where he is allowed to just cut loose & get messy. These are perfect!

P.S. if you are concerned that teaching them to color on surfaces is a bad or confusing message, which makes perfect sense...I'd say that this is the way to let them be creative & have a blast but teach them that coloring on wall is only for the bathtub and only with these crayons....a concept they will need to learn.

I would recommend getting your first set somewhere that you can return them if they don't work on your tub. Also, get a matte finish silicone baking mat, or matte silicone placemat...wet the back, stick to wall & let them color on that. It works great for us!
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Deluxe (EA) The special part of this particular version of Scrabble is the fact that the case is also the game. It's easy to keep everything together with this case, and it has grip-like places at the top that make toting the case around easy.

The case is hard plastic and it simply unfolds to reveal the game board, which is also plastic. The board is designed so that the tiles are placed within a square spot, and won't move around or get jarred out of place easily. Wheels are attached to the bottom(or each side of the case) to make turning the board in a circle easier. If the player wants to pull the board towards them, these wheels won't make that task easier. The wheels are turned a bit, making the board turn in a circle, not a line.

On each side of the case are drawers that pull out. These drawers are actually pretty roomy. These hold the tiles and the tile holders. The tile holders are plastic, and come within a velvet-like drawstring bag. The tiles are wooden.

Overall, this isn't the prettiest or fanciest of games. Despite being called "Deluxe", don't expect a glamorous version. It IS designed to make playing scrabble a little easier, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Deluxe (EA)

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game We just aren't overly fond of this game. It ended up being super frustrating for us.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.

Thomas & Friends Wood, Gordon This Gordon set comes with the engine and his "tender" coal car. The first thing I noticed was the strong smell of paint or stain coming from the train even while it was still in the package. The smell was worse after the train was removed from the package. The train is mainly made of beech wood. The decoration is painted on except for the plastic face. The car and the tender connect using magnets. The train's head, the wheels, and part of the connector is made from plastic. The axles are metal. The engine is 3" long, 2" tall, and 1.5" wide. The tender is 2.25" long, 1.75" tall, and 1.5" wide. The train was smaller than I expected, and I didn't care for the strong smell though I'm sure it will dissipate with time. The train can be used on the floor without a track if desired. From the packaging: "2+. Made in China. 100% wood from well-managed forests. This product contains magnets. Do not use around items that are sensitive to or affected by magnetic fields."

I also received an adapter track pack, but I'm not sure if that was because I'm an Amazon Vine reviewer or if it comes with the engine. I don't have any of the old, wooden track, so I don't actually need these adapters. However, since I have no track, I used these as my main track. When I put the eight included pieces together, the track was about 16" long. The track is very easy to slot together. The track is plastic and each piece is 2.25" long, just over 1.5" wide, and 0.5" thick. The included advertising says that the new Thomas and Friends wood trains are compatible with the old track and the redesign track can be connected to the classic track using the two adapter pieces included with every product that contains track. "Made in China. Not suitable for children under 36 months."
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends Wood, Gordon

Marvel Guardians of the Galaxy Dancing Groot This is a simple toy. It's not something to entertain a modern child with for more than a few minutes, not even enough time to go through the demo batteries. The sound is reasonable and there are a few song bites from the soundtrack. I have had no problems getting him to pick up sound even from some distance. He dances to my terrible singing. Gotta love that. His arms are poseable, moving like most action figures, up, down and some lateral movement. The eyes light up and he speaks. He has a shutoff switch to save battery life.The bottom half of the body slides across surfaces and will eventually find the edge. Something to watch for since I doubt he bounces well.

All that being said...

I think this little guy is absolutely adorable. He is now Guardian of the Residence and shows up all over the house, much like that little Christmas elf. I may even end up making him clothes. And every Baby Groot needs his own mini teddy bear from the craft store.

This has been goofy and fun for me and well worth having around.

I AM GROOT!

VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys Oh, what have I done?

I bought Patrick the Pygmy Goat as a gift for my goat loving wife this past Christmas. Upon seeing it Christmas morning, her eyes lit up and she took to it immediately. I thought I had made the perfect choice.

Or so I thought.

I quickly found that it seems Patrick was always watching me. At night, he would sit atop the pillows on the bed watching over his new domain. Despite the fact his head seems to be affixed to only look to his left, it still seems he is looking at me no matter what side of the bed I’m on. When I tuck in my wife at night, he is there staring. When I come back from brushing my teeth, he is there staring. When I lift the sheets to turn over at night, he is there staring into my soul.

I’m pretty sure he is plotting against me. I can see him in the window looking down at me when I take the trash out to the street. I get phone calls with the sounds of capra aegagrus hircus breathing on the other end. Sometimes he is there under my feet when walking by or sitting on my chest when I wake.

I’ve spoken to my wife about my concerns, but she laughs them off. I’m starting to think she is in on it with the goat. With Patrick. Even now, he is watching me type.

Despite the above concerns, he appears to be a really great stuffed goat. My wife falls asleep with him in her arms each night as he whispers, whatever it is he is saying, into her ear.
text_fidelity_b: VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys

text_fidelity_a:
Blade Inductrix FPV RTF (Yellow) I am a complete newbie to drones. I've operated one of the Phantom 3 drones that my son owns, which is a completely different animal. So, out of the box, I was completely dependent on the instructions to get me up and running. After looking through the last of five instruction sheets, I finally found the English version. Without going into great detail, I'll just say that it was not easy at all finding and understanding the basic minimum to get you in the air. There is a lot of terminology about components that I had no idea what was being referred to. Example: Three-in-one control unit. It took me considerable time to figure out that the three-in-one control unit is a part of the quad copter itself. Now, it must be acknowledged that this is an unbelievable amount of technology in such a small package. So I guess it's a little much to expect that it would be simple to operate. But after getting the battery charged and after a few trials and errors, I got the copter in the air. The included video screen actually has a reasonably clear picture. And after a lot of practice I got to where I could fly it through my house, upstairs from controlling downstairs and still got good video reception and control. This little unit is built pretty tough. And it needs to be, because, especially if you're a newbie, you'll crash a lot. It really took a beating on my hardwood floors. Carpeted floors would be a lot easier on the equipment. While the drone is very durable and has built in protection for the video camera, I broke several of the stanchions that attach the motors to the circular blade guard. I was able to use instant glue and get back in the air. But the good news is that individual parts are sold separately so it can evidently be fairly easily repaired.

This little drone is very fun to fly. Battery life on the one single included battery is consistently about 3 minutes per flight. It takes about 15 minutes to charge. As has been recommended in several articles I've read, I will be purchasing additional batteries and a gang-charger. I'll give this unit four stars. The value for the price is, I believe, very good. The main frustrating drawback is the lack of more simple and basic instructions. It's far from an "open-the-box-and-fly" unit. But if you have the patience to stick with it and improve your skills, it's tremendously fun to fly!
text_fidelity_b: Blade Inductrix FPV RTF (Yellow)

text_fidelity_a:
Bezier Games One Week Ultimate Werewolf "Werewolf" games from Bezier games are becoming a bit ubiquitous at this point. That said, the core gameplay of the original, and certain spinoff titles like Inquisition have worked well for me in the past. "One Night" never really floated my boat, as it was too short and chaotic, so the "One Week" version seemed like a good fit.

In this game, you're moving around a castle board searching for Werewolves. You can do many "One Night" things - switch tokens without knowing who you are or who you become, and you need to bluff about which cards you are using. Unfortunately, this game shares a little too much from many of the same flaws that I noticed with One Night Ultimate Werewolf - it's too chaotic, it's still too quick, and you still will struggle to make strategic decisions because you don't often know what you are doing when you take actions. For people who enjoy the strategy-less designer games, like Talisman or traditional Werewolf, then this might be a hit if you have the right group.

For the right group, this will be a big success. While I do like it more than "One Night", it's not quite ready for my tastes yet.
text_fidelity_b: Bezier Games One Week Ultimate Werewolf

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary) I bought 2 of these blasters for my daughter and I. We have Nerf battles in the house and She wanted a semi auto (to back up her Recon and Maverick) and I need a backup for the Hail Fire. This is a clip system balster with a fly wheel launcher (need 4 AA batteries). All in all I'm pretty pleased.
Good: This blaster does a lot of things well. It is a semi-auto (requires 4 AA batteries), but does not feel heavy or unbalanced. Easy to shoot 1 handed and can be double wielded. Clip system is nice as we have a lot of extra clips so reloads are fast. The clip release button has a good positive feel and has not accidentally relesed a clip yet. The blaster has a top and bottom tactical rail and will accecpt a stock and barrel extention (although why you would want to do this is questionable as it takes away the intent of this compact blaster). Handgrip is comfortable but may be to small for XL hands. Accel. button has a good feel to it. There are 2 place for sling attachment and both spots are logical! Battery door is a sigle screw affair. Accuracy is better than expected (I can hit a human size target 5 out of 6 times at a 30 foot range). Battery life has been good and Rechargables offer no problems.
Bad: This blaster has more safety switches than a modern Table Saw! There is the jam door switch, the clip sensor switch, dart sensor switch, voltage switch (regulator), accel trigger switch, and probably others that I haven't come across yet. The main trouble maker is the dart sensor switch. It works great until the last dart in the clip. Sometimes the dart pressure is not enough to press the switch arm so the blaster won't fire the last dart (VERY ANNOYING!) The easiest NONE WARRENTY VOIDING fix is to open the jam door, take a thin (about 1/8" wide) piece of duct tape (about 2 inches long) and tape the switch to the top of the reciever. I taped it up and around the body and out the top of the jam door. After aprox 100 shots the tape is still holding and I have yet to have a dart left in the clip. The gun is also prone to jamming if you pull the trigger slowly. When firing off a dart you need to make sure to pull the trigger crisply. This only seems to be a problem on the first shot (probably because I usually empty the clip after that first shot). Another problem I've seen is the dislike this blaster has for non-elite darts. If your first dart in the clip is a streamline version you can almost be assured a jam (funny that it only happens if the non-elite is in the first position on the clip- load it farther down and it fires like any other dart). Honestly if your gonna use this for any formal matches stick to the Elite darts. Range is about 35 to 40 feet- hard to get any further.
Final thoughts: This is truely a fun blaster. It does have a few kinks to it, but nothing that a little duct tape can't fix. It is compact enough to carry as a secondary blaster, but combined with additional clip options (I'm thinking an 18 with a couple six back-ups) this could be a close quarters primary blaster. At the current $20 this is really a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Scientific Explorer Bee-Ology Science Kids Science Experiment Kit This is an interesting kit, that in all fairness should probably be about a 3.5 star product, but Amazon forces me to choose, so I'll rank this on the lower end.

There is a lot to like here - the activities are pretty good, the variety is great, and the educational value is fantastic. My daughter's favorite were the bee goggles, which was the simplest activity, while I liked the idea of building the model to identify the parts of the bee. There are some simple chits that you can move around to organize a hive that look like they belong in a board game, but didn't provide a lot of interest for daughter.

There are plenty of opportunities as well. The book that comes with the set is a big miss. There is a ton of information inside that helped me answer some questions for my daughter, but it is dry as a bone, and holds no interest for her whatsoever. It's essentially an encyclopedia entry about bees, and educationally, it's fabulous, but from a kid's point of view, they forgot to include anything fun.

There is one activity that requires you have a live flower, so that will be a miss for anyone doing this kit over a fall or winter season unless they want to take a separate trip to the store.

As I said above, there were 5 activities, and while I liked one or two, there's not too much to some of them. Pollinate a flower? OK, that's done in a few minutes. Bee wings buzzing? A fun toy, not too much really make use of here. The goggles were a hit with the kid, but are a dress up accessory at best for me. The model was great. The peel and stick bit was a good idea that didn't resonate with my little one.

Overall, it's a good idea, especially given the season we've tried it in, and in combination with our outdoor bee sanctuaries and veggie garden. Giving kids an education about these pollinators is important and could be a fantastic idea for the future, but for this kit, I think there's room for improvement.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Scientific Explorer Bee-Ology Science Kids Science Experiment Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

I love that it covers what you’d expect with matching letters, but also includes other things like rhyming, what happens next themes, letters that start and end in certain sounds, as well as other concepts.

Two areas of improvement: The Pen—My child tends to hold it in the middle or more toward the top, and the sound button always seems to get turned off. I don’t really know of a better placement for this button, but it’s worth mentioning. Maybe one of those slider buttons would be better at preventing the sound being turned off so easily.

The dots themselves don't seem very small, but still seem to cause us some issues when in use. Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Hot Dots Let's Learn Pre-K Reading - Learn to Read Preschool Workbook with Interactive Pen, Kids Travel Activity, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs We've been making potholders at home and it seemed like we were always running out of the colors we wanted, so we ordered replacements from several different sources to see what worked best. Although these are not the easiest to use, they by far make the best finished product. This is a great big bag of loops with very vibrant colors. The colors are great -- teal, cobalt, lime green, kelly green, pink, red, reddish-purple, yellow, orange -- enough to make some beautiful combinations. Compared to the other loops we've used, these are very thick and less stretchy. Because they are bulkier, they are a little harder to work with. I haven't found any that don't fit, though. On the flip side, the finished potholder is larger and holds its shape better. I've found that the stretchier brands seem to have a lot of nylon, and it doesn't seem like they'd hold up as well to hot dishes. These loops are kind of scraggly, with loose threads hanging off of them, but when you weave them together the loose threads aren't really a problem.

Someone commented that her daughter wasn't able to weave the edges with these because they were less stretchy. My daughter hasn't been able to weave the edges with these either, but she's very, very proud of the finished product as it is larger, more vibrant, and more even in shape than the potholders made with the stretchier loops.

If you want something that's really easy to use, you might check for the loops made by klutz or others, as these might not be the best bet. If you want to make cool potholders, though, these are a good choice.

UPDATE: I'm back a year later to buy more. Glad that I was able to find the good loops again. And now that my daughter is 8, she no longer has difficulty weaving the edges -- most of the time. Also, these are much easier to weave off the edges when you use the metal loom, rather than the plastic ones.

UPDATE #2: Almost two years later, and my daughter is back making potholders, this time trying to create her own designs. Need more loops!
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs

The foot pads are wide enough that you don't slip off and the padded handlebars are great in case you topple to one side and accidentally bonk yourself in the face. (Hey, it happens!)

This stick is for beginners that are just learning. It takes about 2 days for a child to learn to pogo, especially if they are tall or longer-legged. Start on a very flat surface (not a slanted driveway) and encourage them to be patient as they learn how to balance on it. And once you learn, you never forget! But don't try it, dad - this pogo smashes pretty flat if an adult tries to use it because it's only rated to 80 pounds! (Might handle 90 lbs okay.) Soon they'll be able to do several bounces in a row and, before you're completely comfortable with the idea, they'll be taking massive leaps on the thing, galloping down the cul-de-sac!

Incredibly fun outdoor toy in a bright color that helps you spot it so you don't run it over if it's left out in the driveway!
